statements.label: supported
statements.text: In medaka, all three pigment cell types, melanophores, xanthophores and leucophores, fail to form without functional Mitf.
statements.evidence: Similarly, medaka Mitf is necessary for melanophore, xanthophore and leucophore formation.
statements.note: The abstract states that medaka Mitf is necessary for the formation of all three of these cell types.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In zebrafish the regulatory links among Sox10, Pax3 and Mitf are conserved, and Mitf additionally shapes xanthophore development.
statements.evidence: Here, we show that the regulatory relationships between Sox10, Pax3 and Mitf are conserved in zebrafish, but the role for Mitf is more complex than previously emphasized, affecting xanthophore development too.
statements.note: This is the abstract's central zebrafish result: the three-factor relationships hold, and Mitf also affects xanthophores.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Iridophore development in zebrafish requires Pax7.
statements.evidence: In teleosts, which have three to four pigment cell types (melanophores, iridophores and xanthophores, plus leucophores e.g. in medaka), gene regulatory networks governing fate specification are poorly understood, although Mitf function is considered conserved.
statements.note: Iridophores appear only in the list of teleost pigment cell types; the abstract reports nothing about what specifies them.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Pax7 steers cells that co-express it with Mitf toward xanthophore and leucophore identity rather than melanophore identity.
statements.evidence: Pax7 modulates Mitf function, driving co-expressing cells to differentiate as xanthophores and leucophores rather than melanophores.
statements.note: The abstract reports exactly this effect of Pax7 on co-expressing cells.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Xbp1 and Brachyury regulate one another, forming a cross-regulatory subcircuit of the notochord network that has been conserved through chordate evolution.
statements.evidence: We report the regulatory interplay between Xbp1 and Brachyury, and by extending these results to Xenopus , we show that Brachyury and Xbp1 form a cross-regulatory subcircuit of the notochord gene regulatory network that has been consolidated during chordate evolution.
statements.note: The abstract reports the Xbp1-Brachyury interplay and the subcircuit consolidated over chordate evolution.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genes placed downstream of Xbp1 in the Ciona notochord include unfolded protein response genes, indicating early recruitment of that pathway into notochord development.
statements.evidence: Through the identification of Xbp1-downstream notochord genes in Ciona , we found evidence of the early co-option of genes involved in the unfolded protein response to the notochord developmental program.
statements.note: The abstract describes the early co-option of unfolded protein response genes into the notochord program.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Mutations in human XBP1 cause congenital malformations of the spine.
statements.evidence: We are using a simple chordate model, the Ciona embryo, to investigate the essential gene regulatory network that orchestrates morphogenesis of the notochord, a structure necessary for the proper development of all chordate embryos.
statements.note: The abstract works in Ciona and Xenopus embryos and says nothing about human XBP1 variants or any human phenotype.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Xbp1 is a transcription factor whose expression accompanies notochord formation in Ciona as well as in other chordates.
statements.evidence: Here, we focus on Xbp1, a transcription factor expressed during notochord formation in Ciona and other chordates.
statements.note: The abstract introduces Xbp1 as a transcription factor expressed during notochord formation in Ciona and other chordates.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Across the Metazoa, CNEs arise repeatedly around the same genes, among them homeodomain genes and other transcription factors, and around genes for neural development.
statements.evidence: We show that CNEs evolve repeatedly around the same genes across the Metazoa, including around homeodomain genes and other transcription factors; they also evolve repeatedly around genes involved in neural development.
statements.note: The abstract states both the repeated evolution around the same genes and the neural development genes.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Deleting a transposon-derived CNE in a cnidarian disrupts neural patterning in the embryo.
statements.evidence: they also evolve repeatedly around genes involved in neural development.
statements.note: The abstract locates CNEs near neural development genes but reports no deletion experiment or resulting phenotype.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Hundreds of thousands of CNEs were identified across more than 50 genomes drawn from Cnidaria, Mollusca and Arthropoda.
statements.evidence: we conducted a large-scale characterization of CNEs in more than 50 genomes from three of the main branches of the metazoan tree: Cnidaria, Mollusca, and Arthropoda. We identified hundreds of thousands of CNEs
statements.note: The abstract gives both the genome count and the order of magnitude of the CNE set.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transposons are a major source of CNEs in these invertebrate genomes, in line with what had been seen previously in vertebrates.
statements.evidence: We also show that transposons are a major source of CNEs, confirming previous observations from vertebrates
statements.note: The abstract reports transposons as a major CNE source and notes the agreement with earlier vertebrate work.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Experimental disruption of an ultraconserved element in mice produces visible skeletal defects.
statements.evidence: The definition was subsequently extended to sequences ≥ 100 bp identical in at least three of five mammalian genomes (including dog and cow), and shown to have undergone rapid expansion from ancestors in fish and strong negative selection in birds and mammals.
statements.note: Selection on these elements is inferred from sequence comparisons; the abstract describes no experiment that removes an element from any organism.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Ultraconserved elements sit mostly in introns of protein-coding and noncoding genes tied to neurological and skeletomuscular development, and are enriched in regulatory elements.
statements.evidence: Ultraconserved elements are mainly located in the introns of protein-coding and noncoding genes involved in neurological and skeletomuscular development, enriched in regulatory elements, and dynamically expressed throughout embryonic development.
statements.note: The abstract's closing sentence gives their intronic location, the gene categories and the enrichment for regulatory elements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Under the updated definition of 100 bp length and 97% identity in half of placental mammal orders, the dedUCE pipeline yields 12,813 ultraconserved elements.
statements.evidence: We suggest an updated definition of ultraconserved elements as sequences ≥ 100 bp and ≥97% sequence identity in ≥50% of placental mammal orders (12,813 ultraconserved elements).
statements.note: The abstract gives the proposed thresholds together with the resulting count of 12,813 elements.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mapping to about 200 species places the appearance of placental ultraconserved elements early in vertebrate evolution, well ahead of land colonization.
statements.evidence: By mapping ultraconserved elements to ∼200 species, we find that placental ultraconserved elements appeared early in vertebrate evolution, well before land colonization
statements.note: The abstract dates their appearance from the mapping across roughly 200 species.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ApoD2 is strongly expressed in lepidopteran wings and encodes a unique C-terminal tail that gives it distinct ligand-binding properties.
statements.evidence: Notably, duplicated ApoD2 was highly expressed in lepidopteran wings and encoded a unique C-terminal tail, conferring distinct ligand-binding properties.
statements.note: The abstract reports the wing expression, the unique tail and the resulting ligand-binding properties.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In Bombyx mori, duplicated ApoD2 mediates lipid trafficking and lipid homeostasis in the wing through the AMPK pathway.
statements.evidence: Using Bombyx mori as a model organism, we integrated evolutionary analysis, multiomics, and in vivo functional experiments to elucidate the way duplicated ApoD2 mediates lipid trafficking and homeostasis via the AMP-activated protein kinase pathway in wings.
statements.note: The abstract names the pathway through which ApoD2 acts on wing lipid trafficking and homeostasis.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The ApoD gene family expanded in insects, and the duplicates were consistently retained in Lepidoptera.
statements.evidence: ApoD underwent significant expansion in insects, with gene duplication and consistent retention observed in Lepidoptera.
statements.note: The abstract reports the insect-wide expansion of ApoD and the consistent retention of duplicates in Lepidoptera.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Silencing ApoD2 shortens the flight distance of adult Bombyx mori moths.
statements.evidence: Owing to the diversification of insect wing morphology and dynamic energy requirements, the molecular adaptation mechanisms underlying the metabolic pathways in wing evolution remain largely unknown.
statements.note: The abstract frames wing energy demands and measures lipid regulation, but no flight performance of any kind is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The Oryza data indicate that de novo genes feed the rapid evolution of protein diversity under positive selection.
statements.evidence: These data reveal that de novo genes contribute to the rapid evolution of protein diversity under positive selection.
statements.note: This is the conclusion the abstract draws from its de novo gene set.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A minimum of 175 de novo open reading frames were found in Oryza sativa subspecies japonica, every one of them present in RNA-sequencing transcriptomes.
statements.evidence: we detected at least 175 de novo open reading frames in the focal species O. sativa subspecies japonica, which were all detected in RNA sequencing-based transcriptomes.
statements.note: The abstract gives the count of open reading frames and states that all were seen in the transcriptome data.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The de novo genes found in japonica are absent from the genomes of cultivated maize.
statements.evidence: High-quality genomes of 13 closely related Oryza species provide unprecedented opportunities to understand de novo origination events.
statements.note: The comparisons in the abstract stay inside the genus Oryza; no species outside it is examined.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Targeted proteomics by mass spectrometry and ribosomal profiling support translation for 57% of the de novo genes.
statements.evidence: Mass spectrometry-based targeted proteomics and ribosomal profiling show translational evidence for 57% of the de novo genes.
statements.note: The abstract reports translational evidence for this share of the de novo genes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Deep transcriptomics combined with synteny across several yeast species, grown under two conditions, identified 213 de novo transcripts in Saccharomyces cerevisiae.
statements.evidence: Here, we identify 213 de novo originated transcripts in Saccharomyces cerevisiae using deep transcriptomics and genomic synteny information from multiple yeast species grown in two different conditions.
statements.note: The abstract gives the number of transcripts and the data used to find them.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The small proteins translated from these de novo transcripts raise yeast survival at high temperature.
statements.evidence: Thus, a large fraction of de novo genes in yeast are likely to co-evolve with already existing genes.
statements.note: The abstract ends on co-evolution with neighbouring genes; no fitness or survival measurement appears anywhere in it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Yeast de novo transcripts frequently emerge from regions that already harbour another gene in the opposite orientation.
statements.evidence: We find that about half of the de novo transcripts are expressed from regions which already harbor other genes in the opposite orientation
statements.note: About half of the transcripts overlap an existing gene on the opposite orientation, as the abstract states.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Under stress, the overlapping de novo transcripts change expression much as the genes they overlap do, and some of them appear to make small proteins.
statements.evidence: these transcripts show similar expression changes in response to stress as their overlapping counterparts, and some appear to translate small proteins.
statements.note: The abstract reports both the shared stress response and the apparent translation of small proteins.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Female flies carrying atlas mutations show impaired fertility.
statements.evidence: Many such genes are expressed in male reproductive tissues, but their functions remain poorly understood.
statements.note: The screen and every assay in the abstract concern male reproductive tissue and male fertility; females are never tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: A screen of more than 40 putative de novo genes with testis-enriched expression in Drosophila melanogaster singled out atlas as needed for male fertility.
statements.evidence: we conducted a functional genetic screen of over 40 putative de novo genes with testis-enriched expression in Drosophila melanogaster and identified one gene, atlas, required for male fertility.
statements.note: The abstract describes the screen, its size and the single gene it identified.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Within about the last 15 million years atlas relocated to an autosome, fused with a non-coding RNA, and acquired a non-redundant role in male fertility.
statements.evidence: Within the last ~15 million years, however, the gene moved to an autosome, where it fused with a conserved non-coding RNA and evolved a non-redundant role in male fertility.
statements.note: The abstract dates the move to an autosome and the fusion that gave atlas its non-redundant role.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Atlas protein appears in spermatid nuclei and enables the switch from histone-based to protamine-based chromatin packaging late in spermatogenesis.
statements.evidence: Atlas protein is expressed in spermatid nuclei and facilitates the transition from histone- to protamine-based chromatin packaging.
statements.note: The abstract reports the nuclear localisation and the role in the histone-to-protamine transition.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Roughly 2,000 of the screened random genes promoted growth of Escherichia coli cells producing the MazF toxin.
statements.evidence: We identified ~2,000 genes that could promote growth, probably by reducing transcription from the promoter driving toxin expression.
statements.note: The abstract gives this number of random genes that let the toxin-producing cells grow.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: One random protein, RamF, interacted with chaperones and reset protein homeostasis, which led to MazF proteolysis and the end of its toxicity.
statements.evidence: Additionally, one random protein, named Random antitoxin of MazF (RamF), modulated protein homeostasis by interacting with chaperones, leading to MazF proteolysis and a consequent loss of its toxicity.
statements.note: The abstract describes this chain from chaperone interaction to MazF proteolysis and loss of toxicity.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Mutations identified in RamF turned it into a more efficient inhibitor, showing that random proteins can improve over the course of evolution.
statements.evidence: Finally, we demonstrate that random proteins can improve during evolution by identifying beneficial mutations that turned RamF into a more efficient inhibitor.
statements.note: The abstract reports beneficial mutations that made RamF a more efficient inhibitor.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: RamF also protects Escherichia coli against antibiotic stress.
statements.evidence: Our work provides a mechanistic basis for how de novo gene birth can produce functional proteins that effectively benefit cells evolving under stress.
statements.note: The only stress in the abstract is MazF toxin expression; no antibiotic or other challenge is tested.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In Raleigh inbred lines, some candidates with low expression frequency represent deleterious transcription promoted by inbreeding depression.
statements.evidence: We find evidence from genetic analysis of Raleigh inbred lines that a fraction of rarely expressed gene candidates in this population represent deleterious transcription promoted by inbreeding depression.
statements.note: The abstract attributes a fraction of the rarely expressed candidates in this population to inbreeding depression.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Most of the newly reported de novo gene candidates are expressed polymorphically, and many of them are predicted to encode secreted proteins.
statements.evidence: We report a large number of previously undiscovered de novo gene candidates, most of which are expressed polymorphically. Many are predicted to code for secreted proteins.
statements.note: The abstract states both the polymorphic expression of most candidates and the prediction of secreted proteins.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The secreted proteins predicted from these candidates function in sperm competition.
statements.evidence: Many de novo gene candidates are expressed in multiple tissues and both sexes, raising questions about how they may interact with natural selection.
statements.note: The abstract leaves the role of selection open and reports no functional test of any candidate protein.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Zambian and North American populations express comparable numbers of candidate de novo genes even though their levels of genomic variation differ markedly.
statements.evidence: In spite of much different levels of genomic variation in Zambian and North American populations, they express similar numbers of candidate de novo genes.
statements.note: The abstract reports similar candidate counts in the two populations despite their different variation levels.
